## Research Fields

::: {.cv-plain}
Empirical asset pricing (cross-sectional return prediction, factor models); financial econometrics (identification and inference in high-dimensional factor models); portfolio choice and risk management; machine learning and big data in finance.
:::

## Positions

:::: {.cv-row}
::: {.cv-when}
Jun 2026–present
:::
::: {.cv-what}
**Visiting Researcher**, Imperial Centre of Excellence in Quantitative Finance, Department of Finance, Imperial Business School, Imperial College London

[Host: [Prof. Robert Kosowski](https://profiles.imperial.ac.uk/r.kosowski), Co-Director of the Centre]{.cv-sub}

[Research agenda for the visit: economically constrained machine learning for cross-sectional asset pricing and systematic investment.]{.cv-sub}

- Machine learning and asset pricing: building no-arbitrage restrictions into the learning of latent factors rather than testing them afterwards; extending the thesis's No-Arbitrage IPCA framework to regime-switching factor models in which risk premia vary with macro conditions.
- High-dimensional data: combining penalised estimation with economically constrained representation learning to separate robust alpha signals from those driven by weak factors or data snooping.
- Research and practice: using the Student Investment Fund's quantitative platform to test research signals as implementable strategies under transaction-cost, turnover and risk limits.
:::

:::

**AI and Machine-Learning Adviser** (part-time), Cost of Capital team, Infrastructure Advisory, [KPMG LLP (UK)](https://kpmg.com/uk/en.html)

- Academic advice on machine-learning methods and on the robust use of asset-pricing models, such as the conditional CAPM and the betting-against-beta (BAB) factor, in independent estimates of the allowed cost of equity for regulated UK utilities (water and energy networks).

## Research

### Job Market Paper

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions](/research/characteristic-libraries.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[Develops an empirical framework that judges updates to the characteristic library of a machine-learning portfolio by their investment consequences, using controls that add no information (duplicated or re-weighted themes) to separate re-weighting of existing signals from new information.]{.cv-sum}
:::

### Working Papers

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[SSRN preprint, September 2026. DOI: [10.2139/ssrn.7445120](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7445120)]{.cv-pmeta}

[Shows that the inner product placed on characteristic space determines how models with identical fit split expected returns among latent factors, observed factors and an intercept, and develops coordinate-free inference when this metric is estimated from data.]{.cv-sum}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models](/research/geometric-framework.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[SSRN preprint, March 2026. DOI: [10.2139/ssrn.7013178](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7013178)]{.cv-pmeta}

[Measures characteristics with an empirical metric derived from their long-run cross-sectional distribution, states identification and no-arbitrage restrictions as geometric properties, and proposes No-Arbitrage IPCA (NA-IPCA), which nests IPCA and admits rotation-invariant inference.]{.cv-sum}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice](/research/characteristic-geometry.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[Traces why factor models with almost identical return forecasts hold different portfolios to a fixed ridge adjustment to factor variance, which penalises exposures differently across loading representations, and proposes comparing models under a common risk adjustment.]{.cv-sum}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts](/research/interpreting-pricing-errors.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[Separates changes in fitted expected returns from changes in factor loading spaces to ask what a smaller estimated pricing error tells a model user and whether pricing-error diagnostics help in choosing or adjusting a return forecast.]{.cv-sum}
:::

### PhD Thesis

::: {.cv-paper}
[*No-Arbitrage IPCA: A Framework for Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing*]{.cv-ptitle}

[Imperial College London; PhD conferred August 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[Develops an empirical characteristic metric and a nested sequence of models (IPCA, QZ-IPCA and NA-IPCA) that separates latent, observable and residual pricing components, with identification results, asymptotic theory and an estimation algorithm.]{.cv-sum}
:::

## Research Experience

:::: {.cv-row}
::: {.cv-when}
Aug 2019–present
:::
::: {.cv-what}
**Doctoral research**, Department of Finance, Imperial College London (asset pricing and quantitative finance)

- Cross-sectional asset pricing: models for 12,813 US stocks and 153 characteristics (1964–2025) that combine latent and observable factors under no-arbitrage restrictions; out-of-sample comparison with PCA, IPCA and Fama–French models, with risk decomposition and cost-aware backtests.
- Data: 153 characteristics built from CRSP/Compustat with rolling windows and point-in-time alignment, controlling for survivorship and look-ahead bias; additional data from WRDS, Bloomberg and LSEG.
- Macro regimes and cross-asset allocation: hidden Markov and state-space models of inflation, liquidity-stress, risk-off and recovery regimes across equities, rates, FX, commodities and volatility.
- Machine learning and text: transfer learning that builds economic restrictions into neural networks (pre-training on synthetic data, fine-tuning on real data); transformer and topic models that extract risk exposures from 10-K filings, earnings calls and macro news.
:::
::::

:::: {.cv-row}
::: {.cv-when}
May 2018–May 2019
:::
::: {.cv-what}
**Research Assistant (macro forecasting)**, Department of Economics, Columbia University

- Diffusion-index and factor models that extract common inflation and interest-rate factors from large mixed-frequency macro data; robust PCA and stable principal component pursuit for missing data, revisions, outliers and structural breaks.
:::
::::

:::: {.cv-row}
::: {.cv-when}
Jun 2016–Jan 2017
:::
::: {.cv-what}
**Research Assistant (derivatives pricing)**, Department of Mathematics, University of Michigan

- Real-option valuation of a gold mine, using the Lihir Gold Limited IPO as a case: estimated gold-price volatility and the present value of total costs, took strike parameters from the prospectus, and priced the option with a binomial tree.
:::
